new_candidates.body:
### Description

With `ROS2ControlManager` (the `IsaacSimSystem` hardware interface from `isaacsim.ros2.control`) running on an official Jetbot, the robot slowly rotates and translates while idle. No controller is loaded and no command is sent. The same scene wired with the topic approach (`ROS2SubscribeJointState` -> `IsaacArticulationController`), or with no graph at all, stays still.

Searched existing issues (open and closed) in this repo for `ros2.control`, `ROS2ControlManager`, `IsaacSimSystem`, drift/idle/wheel keywords, and the `isaacsim.ros2.control` CHANGELOG (0.1.0 to 0.1.6, identical in v6.2.0 and main). I found no report of this. #915 is about URDF pruning and looks unrelated.

### Minimal reproduction

1. Load the official Jetbot USD (default drives, no modifications).
2. Create an OmniGraph with `OnPlaybackTick` -> `ROS2ControlManager` (`targetPrim` = Jetbot root, `controllerConfig` = a YAML listing the controllers), plus `ROS2PublishClock` fed from simulation time (the probe script includes it; it was not isolated separately).
3. Press Play. Do not load any controller (`ros2 control load_controller` is never called) and publish nothing.
4. Step 5940 physics updates (dt = 1/60, about 99 s of sim time), logging the root pose and the wheel joint velocities (`SingleArticulation.get_joint_velocities()`) once per 60 updates.

### Expected

Root pose and wheel velocities stay near zero, as in the controls below.

### Actual (about 99 s sim time, 5940 updates)

| Condition | root (x, y) [m] | yaw [rad] | wheel qd [rad/s] |
|---|---|---|---|
| ROS2ControlManager, no controller, no command | (0.0493, 0.0115) | 0.4269 | (0.283, 0.169), stays in 0.3-0.6 range |
| Topic approach (ROS2SubscribeJointState -> IsaacArticulationController), no command | (0.0003, 0.0) | 0.0037 | (0.0, 0.0), reaches 0 within about 1 s |
| No graph (240 updates) | (0.0003, 0.0) | 0.0037 | (0.0, 0.0) |

Yaw drift is about 0.0042 rad/s (about 0.25 rad/min). Wheel qd at n=0 is 0.58 / 0.61 with ROS2ControlManager and does not decay.

### Things ruled out

1. Command initial values: physics tensor reads show velocity target 0.0, position target 0.0, applied effort 0.0.
2. Drive gains: kp 0, kd 10000 for all three conditions. Re-writing the same gains with `set_gains` at n=600 changes nothing.
3. Which controller is loaded: none, only `joint_state_broadcaster`, velocity controller, and diff_drive give identical results to 4 decimals.
4. Zero command: sending `[0.0, 0.0]` (velocity controller) or an empty Twist (diff_drive) does not change the drift.
5. Non-zero then zero: after driving at `[3.0, 3.0]`, sending `[0.0, 0.0]` brings wheel speed back to about 0.3 rad/s and yaw keeps increasing at about 0.0041 rad/s.
6. Physics settings: `SimulationManager` dt = 1/60 and device = cpu in both setups; forcing `setup_simulation(dt=1/60, device="cpu")` still drifts (different direction and size).
7. Interface mode: `ros2 control list_hardware_interfaces` shows the wheel velocity interfaces as claimed once a velocity controller is loaded, so it is not a missing interface switch.

### Observations (not root cause)

- Wheel joint position `q` changes only about 0.007-0.022 rad/s while idle, much less than the reported qd of 0.3-0.6 rad/s, so the velocity readout may itself be inconsistent with the motion (or my readout method is at fault).
- The `IsaacSimSystem` C++ source is not in the image, so I could not inspect its per-step write path.

### Environment

- Isaac Sim 6.2.0-rc.15 (the `isaacsim.ros2.control` CHANGELOG is unchanged at 0.1.6 in v6.2.0 and main)
- Extension: `isaacsim.ros2.control` 0.1.6, ROS 2 Humble (bundled with the extension)
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04 (container)
- GPU: RTX 5090
- Driver: 580.178.04

### Logs

No errors or warnings related to this are printed. The probe script and time series are available on request.
